subject: Continuity evidence and cutover sequencing — Sentinel Bank RFP
messages:
From: Procurement (Sentinel Bank) <procurement@sentinelbank.com>

Subject: Sentinel Bank RFP — BCP clarifications

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the RFP submission so far. The review team had a few follow-ups specifically around business continuity and failover sequencing we need clarified before moving to commercial review: 

1) Please provide RTO and RPO targets for the following components: control plane, hosted inference (multi-tenant), dedicated pools, and private/VPC deployments.
2) Describe the multi-region failover sequence you would execute for a site-level outage in us-east-1 affecting both compute and regional network (what switches first, how do you preserve in-flight requests, expected client impact windows).
3) Who performs DNS cutover and what are your recommended TTLs?
4) Evidence: any runbook excerpts, previous DR test dates/results, and logs/audit artifacts you can share.

We appreciate concise, actionable answers; the compliance team will include your responses in our due-diligence packet. Can you get this to us by next Wednesday (2027-11-17)?

Regards,
Alice Foster
Senior Procurement Manager
Sentinel Bank
procurement@sentinelbank.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Foster <alice.foster@sentinelbank.com>, Procurement (Sentinel Bank) <procurement@sentinelbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2027 11:08:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Sentinel Bank RFP — BCP clarifications

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Attached are a short exhibit and a sequencing runbook extract; below is a concise matrix and a high-level multi-region sequence tailored to Sentinel’s requirements. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if you prefer.

High-level RTO / RPO (target commitments)
- Control plane (API management, auth): RTO target 15 minutes; RPO near-zero for metadata via multi-region replication of configuration and audit logs.
- Hosted inference (shared/hosted API): RTO target 10–30 minutes (automatic routing + warm standby depending on region); RPO: near-zero for request routing and audit logs; model state is read-only (models are replicated), KV caches are best-effort (RPO ~last checkpoint, typically <2 minutes for persisted caches).
- Dedicated pools (reserved GPU capacity): RTO target 30–90 minutes depending on committed warm capacity and pre-warmed images; RPO: zero for persistent customer data (we replicate control-plane customer configs and model artifacts), KV caches are transient (RPO dependent on application-level persistence).
- Private/VPC deployments (customer-managed infra): RTO & RPO are dependent on customer infra; Redwood provides runbooks, orchestration tooling, and recommended replication patterns — we estimate typical cutover 60–180 minutes for cold on-prem recovery.

Multi-region failover (high-level sequence)
1) Detection: automated health probes and region-level alarms trigger incident.
2) Assessment & policy decision: smart-routing policy checks (latency, capacity, SLA tier) — automatic for hosted customers with failover policy ‘auto’; manual approval for dedicated unless pre-approved.
3) Route reconfiguration: update regional router + CDN edge rules, and adjust DNS (we recommend low TTL during planned maintenance; see below).
4) Capacity allocation: promote warm standby nodes in target region; for Dedicated, if warm capacity not available, trigger autoscale to reserved/burst pools and notify ops.
5) Request draining: active nodes attempt graceful drain; in-flight requests completed where possible, otherwise retried by client after 5xx responses.
6) KV cache and model artifacts: artifacts are replicated to target region; KV caches rebuild from persisted checkpoints and from prefix cache where supported.
7) Validation & canary: traffic routed to 1–5% to run validation, then progressively ramp.
8) Post-cutover monitoring + rollback hooks: automated metrics + manual rollback trigger if error thresholds exceeded.

DNS / TTL guidance
- Recommended TTL during normal ops: 300s (5m) for routing endpoints to allow reasonably quick cutover.
- For planned maintenance, reduce to 60s 12–24 hours before the window.
- Redwood can coordinate with your network team; we perform cutover orchestration but final DNS change is typically controlled by the customer. We can host a failover CNAME under our routing domain for faster control if preferred.

Evidence & attachments included
- redwood-bcp-exhibit.pdf (summary of test history and roles)
- rto-rpo-metrics.xlsx (breakdown by component and observed median times from last full-scale test)
- runbook-cutover-sequence.txt (sequenced checklist + escalation contacts)

Past tests & logs
- Last full-scale regional failover test: 2027-08-14 (summary in redwood-bcp-exhibit.pdf).
- SOC 2 Type II compliance is current — we can provide a statement of applicability and selective logs via an NDA/secure portal.

If you want specific numbers for embeddings workloads or high-throughput streaming workloads we can attach an appendix; otherwise the spreadsheet includes representative values.

Next steps: we can commit to a joint dry-run if you provide an availability window (suggested week of 2027-11-29).

Best,
Soojin Lee
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alice Foster <alice.foster@sentinelbank.com>

Soojin — thanks for the clear write-up and attachments, that helps a lot. Couple of quick clarifications before the packet is finalized: 

1) For embeddings/indexing workloads, what RPO should we expect for partial-loss scenarios (in-flight writes to indexes)?
2) Can you point to the specific audit log retention windows and the mechanism for delivering logs for forensic review in the event of an incident?

Also, the compliance team would like a short mutual action plan (MAP) for a table-top + dry-run we can schedule with you (30–60 minutes prep + a 2–3 hour dry-run). Please propose 2 dates.

Thanks,
Alice

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Foster <alice.foster@sentinelbank.com>, Procurement (Sentinel Bank) <procurement@sentinelbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2027 16:38:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Sentinel Bank RFP — BCP clarifications

Alice — quick answers inline and a proposed MAP below. We can expand the appendix if you need more technical depth.

1) Embeddings/indexing RPO: for streaming writes we recommend an at-least-once ingestion pattern. If an index write fails during regional disruption, our durable write-ahead logs replicate to a cold standby; observed RPO for committed index entries is typically <30 seconds under our supported storage backends. We include client-side retry guidance in the runbook.

2) Audit logs: control-plane audit logs are retained 13 months by default (SOC 2 policy), with options for longer retention as an add-on. Logs are delivered via secure S3 export or direct API pull (signed URLs) — we can set up an automated export to your secure bucket daily.

Proposed MAP (table-top + dry-run)
- Prep (30–60m): review runbook + roles; we’ll share runbook-cutover-sequence.txt and a short slide deck.
- Dry-run (2–3h): simulated region outage, automated failover, canary validation, and rollback exercise.
- Post-mortem (30–45m): review telemetry and open action items.

Proposed dates (please select two options):
- Option A: Tue 2027-11-30 09:00–12:00 ET (prep the day before 11/29)
- Option B: Thu 2027-12-02 13:00–16:00 ET (prep 12/01)

We’ll have Marissa on the call for operational runbook walk-through and Ben for capacity/pricing implications of warm standby. Markus will support any dedicated-pool technical details. If those windows work I’ll send a calendar invite and a pre-read packet.

Best regards,
Soojin
